A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCSF research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including the material added in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original eigensolver timing experiments on four PDE families, sorting and initialization ablations, sensitivity tests, and neural-network training results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds mixture-ratio results, FEM Helmholtz evaluations, and measurements of high-frequency spectral content.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same truncated-FFT sorting, Chebyshev filtering, subspace reuse, and convergence procedures. Expanded explanations of parameter matrices and warm starts do not change the method.

E1.justification: Appendix E.8 extends the evaluated Helmholtz/Poisson mixture populations beyond v1's single 50:50 case, adding unequal mixtures and pure-population controls. The four underlying PDE families and eigenvalue-solving tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The numerical comparators remain Eigsh, LOBPCG, KS, JD, and ChFSI. The neural and sorting comparisons also retain their comparator membership. Table 19 applies the existing numerical comparator set to FEM; newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New Appendix E.10 evaluates FEM/Galerkin Helmholtz matrices of dimension 10,000 at tolerance 1e-8 for 200, 400, and 600 eigenvalues. E.8 introduces a controlled mixture sweep, and E.11 measures high-frequency/total norm ratios at cutoff 20. Existing benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: Supplementary validation expands to two additional questions: sensitivity to discretization in E.10 and whether cutoff 20 retains most spectral content across PDE families in E.11. E.8 also develops the single discontinuous-mixture example into a sweep, substantially broadening the examination of the sorting assumptions.

E5.justification: Section 4.4 newly states that Table 5 averages 100 independent runs. v1 supplies no corresponding repetition count, while the table values remain unchanged; this establishes additional reporting, not an increase in runs. Neither version supplies uncertainty intervals for this comparison.

E6.justification: Tables 1–17 and the original 50:50 mixture results are retained. New results include FEM SCSF times of 116.7, 142.9, and 196.3 seconds in Table 19, additional mixture rows in Table 18, and high-frequency ratios of 3.4–4.8% in Table 20. Section 4.4 also newly reports over 98% agreement between sorting sequences. These supplement the existing results under additional conditions.

T1.justification: New Appendix F introduces mathematical analysis of sorting-distance approximation: normalized-DFT isometry, an exact retained-spectrum/truncation-error decomposition, and Sobolev/spectral-decay assumptions leading to a claimed O(p0^(-2s+d)) tail estimate. This adds direct analytical support for sorting beyond v1's complexity calculations and qualitative motivation, although it is not a complete convergence proof.

C1.justification: The first introduction contribution now qualifies the first-method claim specifically through intrinsic operator similarity and a sorting/filtering framework. This is a limited refinement; the abstract's broader novelty statement, the central acceleration contribution, and the up-to-3.5× speedup claim remain.

C2.justification: Section 5 explicitly discusses non-Hermitian extensions, the fixed Frobenius metric, and failure under discontinuous parameter-to-operator mappings. Section 4.4 adds an explanation for identical sorting-comparison times. E.10–E.11 newly interpret the added results as discretization robustness and retention of over 95% of structural information.

D1.justification: E.10 adds limited technical specifications for the FEM experiment, including Galerkin discretization, matrix dimension, tolerance, and eigenvalue counts; E.11 describes the spectral-ratio calculation. Existing library versions, hardware, SCSF hyperparameters, and eight-core MPI configuration remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on neural operators and eigenproblem acceleration, including Liu et al. (2025a), DeepContour, and STNet. These mainly extend citation support in the introduction and appendices; the related-work narrative and central positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies discretization, parameter matrices, Chebyshev filtering, and warm starts; rewrites parts of Section 4.4; and separates conclusions from limitations. It also updates affiliations and publication headers and adds acknowledgements. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 moves table captions above their tables, adjusts placement and spacing, corrects SCSI to SCSF in plot legends, and clarifies parameter labels in Figure 2. Table 18 gains mixture rows, and Tables 19–20 are added. Existing plots and the general visual design remain substantially intact.

improvement.justification: The expanded mixture analysis, FEM evaluation, and spectral diagnostic provide useful additional evidence about the method's applicability, while clearer limitations and the Table 5 run-count disclosure improve transparency. The gains are limited: the FEM comparison changes matrix size alongside discretization, and Appendix F's stated s > 0 assumption alone does not ensure that its p0^(-2s+d) estimate decays. Overall, the added empirical checks support a modest quality improvement despite these analytical limitations.
